title: What you have and need: einen, keinen (haben, brauchen)
summary: Say what you have, need or don't have. Your first taste of the accusative: ein becomes einen, but only with masculine nouns.
goals: Use haben and brauchen with things
Say einen and keinen with masculine nouns
Say Ich habe keine Zeit and Ich habe Hunger

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 5: Things (Ich habe kein ...)

sections.title: One change: einen
sections.text:
After [[haben]] and [[brauchen]] (and after most verbs), **masculine** [[ein]] becomes **einen**:

- [[Das ist ein Stift.]] but [[Ich brauche einen Stift.]]
- [[Das ist eine Tasche.]] and [[Ich brauche eine Tasche.]] (no change)
- [[Das ist ein Ladegerät.]] and [[Ich brauche ein Ladegerät.]] (no change)

Only the masculine changes, and [[kein]] does the same: [[Ich habe keinen Stift.]] This is the accusative. You will study it properly in Unit 4; for now, learn these as ready-made phrases.

sections.title: ein and kein after haben and brauchen

sections.text: You know the accusative from Russian (Я беру ручку). Funny twist: in Russian the feminine changes (ручка becomes ручку) and a masculine thing stays (стол). In German it is the other way round: [[einen Stift]] changes, [[eine Tasche]] stays. With people both languages change the masculine: [[einen Bruder]], брата.

items.de: Ich habe Hunger. Hast du Durst?

sections.text: German says 'I have hunger' ([[Ich habe Hunger.]]) and 'I have thirst' ([[Ich habe Durst.]]). Russian and Armenian use an adjective here (я голоден, սոված եմ), so don't translate word for word.
[[Ich habe leider keine Zeit.]] (unfortunately) is the polite, very common way to say no to an invitation.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I need a pen.
items.explanation: der Stift is masculine: after brauchen, ein becomes einen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I don't have time.
items.explanation: die Zeit is feminine: keine Zeit (no change).

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Do you have a charger?
items.explanation: das Ladegerät is neuter: ein Ladegerät (no change).

items.question: How do you say 'I'm hungry'?
items.explanation: German says 'I have hunger': Ich habe Hunger. (Ich bin hungrig is also correct, but people say it less. Ich habe hungrig mixes the two and is wrong.)
der Kaffee is masculine, so einen Kaffee.
